reason: The first reading recognised a logical commentary with 'animal rationale mortale' and 'vel sapientibus vel pluribus'; reread with Thomas's text it gave connected lines of lect. 8 on both faces and corrected readings such as 'circulare/exponibilis' to 'circulariter' and 'ex prioribus'.
sources: Thomas Aquinas, Opera omnia iussu Leonis XIII, vol. I (Rome 1882), In libros Posteriorum Analyticorum lib. I lect. 8, pp. 166-170, page images at archive.org operaomniaiussui01thom, leaves n535-n539
Corpus Thomisticum, Expositio libri Posteriorum lib. 1 l. 8 nn. 1-9 (text of the 1882 Leonine edition), https://www.corpusthomisticum.org/cpa1.html

F-jt31 (Stams, Frg. 105): source-assisted reading.
Research readers reread these lines on the image after the source was identified: recto lines 1-5, 8 and 12-24; verso lines 1-5 and 8-24. Recto lines 6-7 and 9-11 (stained) and verso lines 2 and 6-7 (abraded) are read only in part. The words identified there were found with the edition in view.
Expansions are in ( ); [ ] marks text lost at the cut edge or supplied from the edition; (?) marks an uncertain reading.
Canvas 0 = Stams_STA_Frg_105_01r (line-ends survive); canvas 1 = Stams_STA_Frg_105_01v (line-beginnings survive). Boxes are native pixels of the 7360 x 4912 images. The column lies at x 3200-3680 on canvas 0 and x 3370-3830 on canvas 1; line pitch is about 48 px.
